programs.title: Forged in Legend: A Glimpse of Longquan Blades
programs.desc: Longquan swords, legendary blades from China, embody centuries of masterful craftsmanship. Forged with unique folding techniques and a distinctive star-patterned finish, these swords are renowned for their sharpness, resilience, and artistic value. Discover the rich history and cultural significance of these revered symbols of Chinese heritage.

programs.title: Shunde's flavors: where tradition blends with vivid daily life
programs.desc: Shunde, a gastronomic gem in the Pearl River Delta, neighboring Hong Kong, uses masterful craft and sincere heart to transform local treasures - from crispy fish skin to fried milk - into culinary wonders. Now, two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia, are setting out to taste the flavors and feel the warmth of Shunde's countryside with the locals.

programs.title: Foodwise: Changsha
programs.desc: In this episode, our hosts Tianran He and Eva May embark on a journey to Changsha in Hunan Province. They taste their way through the local cuisine, discover the city's latest art and fashion trends, and find out why this place is one of China's "influencer hotspots", attracting millions of domestic and foreign tourists each year.

programs.title: Sweet Planet Ep.4
programs.desc: From China to France, America to India, and beyond - throughout human history, confectionery and desserts have united the world's shared sweet tooth, bringing hope and connection.

programs.title: Jixi 1, Anhui Province
programs.desc: This episode presents the unique charm of Jixi county in Anhui, from the former residence of philosopher Hu shih to brilliant yellow flowering fields of rapeseed in Jiapeng, to a family-run rapeseed oil workshop in the village of Renli, to the sparkling, modern town center.

programs.title: Kungfu-wise: Taiji Quan
programs.desc: Kleber travels to Chenjiagou in central China, the birthplace of Chen-style Taiji Quan. Also known as tai chi, the martial art is iconic for its slow movements and purported health benefits, but Kleber quickly discovers it’s the real deal: From being thrown around by teenagers to learning about the martial art’s Yin-Yang philosophy, Kleber experiences for himself how this kungfu style allows small to defeat big, and soft to beat strong.

programs.title: China IRL podcast: Cooler climes and gentle A/C – Surviving the “Dog Days”
programs.desc: On a filming trip in southwest China’s idyllic Dali prefecture, Travelogue hosts Jack Klumpp, Alex McCutcheon and Tianran He share their tricks for cooling down and keeping healthy through the scorching peak of summer. From heading for the hills, to chowing down on a not-too-cold watermelon, they explore ways to harness the power of Mother Nature and achieve inner coolness. Listen in on this impromptu taxi chat for some useful tips on where to go, what to do, and how to beat the heat this summer!

programs.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.4
programs.desc: In this episode, Tianran He travels to Shannan, the cradle of Tibetan culture. Nestled in the gentlest valley of the Yarlung Zangbo River, this is where the first Tibetan king rose to power, the first palace in Xizang was built, and many other "firsts" in Xizang's history began. Tianran visits Yamdrok Lake, one of Xizang’s three sacred lakes, where a paragliding base is taking shape. He then learns the art of Tibetan opera, joins rangers on a mission to track the elusive Tibetan red deer, and ends the day with a rejuvenating soak in a village revitalized by hot spring tourism.

programs.title: China, Race to the Future Ep.4
programs.desc: This five-episode series explores China's growing cultural confidence, showing how a revival of traditional culture is fueling "chain reactions" that are reshaping Chinese manufacturing and development. In particular, the series stresses how China’s immense cultural capital is empowering a uniquely Chinese approach to building a future that puts openness, globalization and the environment center-stage!

programs.title: A Bite of Xinjiang Ep.4
programs.desc: This is a documentary that comprehensively showcases Xinjiang in all its diversity. Exploring cuisine, landscapes, and folk culture, it shows how diverse ethnic groups drive economic growth, social stability, cultural prosperity, and national unity through diligence and wisdom.

programs.title: Foodwise: Wuzhen
programs.desc: Join our hosts Tianran He and Eva May as they explore the boisterous event of Wuzhen's International Theatre festival, with colorful features of both theatrical and culinary nature. Foodie Tianran and art-lover Eva are accompanied by ubiquitous local street food, daily carnival performances and meet and greets with fascinating personalities. Let's set the stage for the beautiful merge of food and drama as they taste their way through the charming scene of Wuzhen.

programs.desc: This episode uncovers the scenic beauty and cultural depth of Longchuan, a village in Anhui's Jixi county. The presenter observes and learns the manufacturing techniques of Hui ink sticks, and gets a feel for traditional calligraphy.

programs.title: Kungfu-wise: Five Ancestors Fist
programs.desc: In Quanzhou, southeast China, Kleber seeks out masters of the Five Ancestors Fist, a combination of five local kungfu styles. He meets the abbot of a Southern Shaolin Temple, and takes part in the extraordinary training regime used by Shaolin monks to hone their bodies and minds. He experiences the intricacies of Quanzhou's traditional puppetry, and learns how Five Ancestors Fist incorporated military tactics that allowed its practitioners to band together and fight off pirates.

programs.title: Nyingchi Ep.1
programs.desc: In this episode, Tianran He rounds off his travels through Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. He journeys into the Yarlung Zangbo Grand Canyon - one of the largest and deepest canyons on Earth, and along the way, tries to catch a glimpse of Mount Namcha Barwa, the easternmost peak of the Himalayas. Instead, he encounters a waterfall said to be a gateway to the afterlife, before finally arriving at the entrance to the canyon.

Along the way, they uncover the secrets behind its thousand-year legacy and witness the craftsmanship of Xuan paper inheritors at every stage.

programs.title: A Lifelong Journey of Xuan Paper
Celebrating Shuyang Festival in the Longji Rice Terraces
programs.desc: The Longji Rice Terraces in Guangxi are renowned for their magnificent scenery and unique cultural value. Julian Waghann from the United States and Eliza Arce from the Philippines arrived at the cloud-wrapped Longji Rice Terraces to take part in the most solemn annual farming festival: the Shuyang Festival. From the moment they stepped onto the terraces, they walked along the narrow ridges, joined the ancient seedling-combing ritual, sampled distinctive local cuisine, and lifted torches at nightfall to parade and pray with the villagers through the shimmering paddies. Through these vivid scenes, they gradually came to understand the centuries-old symbiotic relationship between the local people and the terraces. The Longji Rice Terraces are not just a breathtaking agricultural panorama - they are a mountain lifestyle and a cultural experience that still breathes today.
